rules.sentence: Certain heritable conditions (fortunately rare) can also cause arrhythmias.
Sudden cardiac death (SCD) is defined as unexpected death due to a lethal arrhythmia such as asystole or sustained ventricular fibrillation.
The prototype is the long QT syndrome, characterized by prolongation of the QT segment in ECGs and susceptibility to malignant ventricular arrhythmias.
Mutations in several different genes account for the cases of long QT syndrome, with KCNQ1 being the most common; it results in decreased potassium currents.
Coronary artery disease is the leading cause of SCD, being responsible for 80% to 90% of cases.
Unfortunately, SCD may be the first manifestation of IHD.
In younger victims of SCD, nonatherosclerotic causes are more common, including the following: Hereditary (channelopathies) or acquired abnormalities of the cardiac conduction system
